definition: A dataset consisting of pairs (or rankings) of model outputs annotated with human (or AI) judgments about which is preferred, used to train reward models or perform direct preference optimization.
details: Preference datasets are central to modern alignment techniques like RLHF and DPO, capturing nuanced human judgments about response quality that are difficult to specify through simple rule-based criteria alone.

explainer.lead: A preference dataset holds pairs or rankings of model outputs annotated with human or AI judgments of preference. It matters as the core data for reward models and direct preference optimization.

tiers.eli5: It's a big collection of side-by-side answers with a note saying which one people liked more.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build these sets to train RLHF and DPO alignment methods. A pitfall is that response quality that is hard to capture in rules must come through human judgment, so annotation design limits the result.
tiers.paperLevel: Data of paired or ranked model outputs with human or AI preference labels, used to train reward models or perform direct preference optimization.

explainer.example: For each prompt, two model outputs are collected and one is marked preferred, forming training data for a reward model.
